expectations.text: Feature code lives in a dedicated feature module (src/features/tasks/...), not in flat top-level folders or App.tsx
expectations.evidence: All task code sits under src/features/tasks/: api/get-tasks.ts, api/create-task.ts, components/create-task.tsx, components/tasks-list.tsx, components/task-list-item.tsx. facts.json lists src/App.tsx under deleted_files, and the route src/app/routes/app/tasks/tasks.tsx only composes feature components ('<CreateTask />', '<TasksList />'). No flat src/api or src/components/tasks folder exists (full src listing verified).

expectations.text: One API file per endpoint under the feature's api/ folder, each exporting a typed fetcher function that uses a shared API client instance
expectations.evidence: Exactly two files in src/features/tasks/api/, one per endpoint. get-tasks.ts: 'export const getTasks = (): Promise<Task[]> => { return api.get('/tasks'); }'. create-task.ts: 'export const createTask = ({ data }: { data: CreateTaskInput }): Promise<Task> => { return api.post('/tasks', data); }'. Both import the shared instance via "import { api } from '@/lib/api-client'", and src/lib/api-client.ts defines a single 'Axios.create({ baseURL: env.API_URL })' with request/response interceptors — no per-file axios instances anywhere.

expectations.text: The list query exports a queryOptions factory and a hook that accepts a queryConfig override parameter (configurable hook)
expectations.evidence: src/features/tasks/api/get-tasks.ts:16-21 'export const getTasksQueryOptions = () => { return queryOptions({ queryKey: ['tasks'], queryFn: () => getTasks() }); }' and lines 23-32 'type UseTasksOptions = { queryConfig?: QueryConfig<typeof getTasksQueryOptions> }; export const useTasks = ({ queryConfig }: UseTasksOptions = {}) => useQuery({ ...getTasksQueryOptions(), ...queryConfig })'. The QueryConfig helper is real, not decorative: src/lib/react-query.ts:20-23 'export type QueryConfig<T extends (...args: any[]) => any> = Omit<ReturnType<T>, 'queryKey' | 'queryFn'>'. The factory is genuinely reused outside the hook — the route loader calls getTasksQueryOptions() to prefetch.

expectations.text: The create mutation validates input with an exported zod schema and its hook accepts a mutationConfig override parameter
expectations.evidence: src/features/tasks/api/create-task.ts:11-16 'export const createTaskInputSchema = z.object({ title: z.string().min(1, 'Required'), description: z.string().min(1, 'Required') }); export type CreateTaskInput = z.infer<typeof createTaskInputSchema>' — the fetcher payload type is derived from the schema. The schema is actually enforced, not just exported: create-task.tsx passes 'schema={createTaskInputSchema}' to Form, and src/components/ui/form/form.tsx:43-59 runs 'const result = schema.safeParse(values)' and returns early on failure. Hook override: 'type UseCreateTaskOptions = { mutationConfig?: MutationConfig<typeof createTask> }' with 'export const useCreateTask = ({ mutationConfig }: UseCreateTaskOptions = {})', and the caller in create-task.tsx supplies 'mutationConfig: { onSuccess: ... }' which is composed rather than clobbered (line 34 destructures onSuccess and re-invokes it after invalidation).

expectations.text: The query key is defined in exactly one place; mutation invalidation reuses the factory's queryKey instead of retyping a string-literal key
expectations.evidence: Repo-wide grep for the literal 'tasks' as a query key returns a single definition: src/features/tasks/api/get-tasks.ts:18 "queryKey: ['tasks'],". Both consumers go through the factory: create-task.ts:38-40 'queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: getTasksQueryOptions().queryKey })' and the route loader src/app/routes/app/tasks/tasks.tsx:17 'queryClient.getQueryData(query.queryKey)'. No string-literal key is retyped anywhere (the only other 'tasks' string is the route path segment in src/config/paths.ts).

expectations.text: No barrel index.ts re-export files anywhere in the new code
expectations.evidence: 'find src -name "index.ts" -o -name "index.tsx"' returns nothing; facts.json new_barrel_index_files is []. Every import in the new code targets a concrete module path, e.g. "import { useTasks } from '@/features/tasks/api/get-tasks'" and "import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button/button'" — deep paths, not folder-level imports.

expectations.text: All new files and folders are kebab-case
expectations.evidence: facts.json non_kebab_new_files is []. Verified against the full src listing: multi-word names are all kebab (not-found.tsx, error-boundary.tsx, field-wrapper.tsx, content-layout.tsx, notifications-store.ts, api-client.ts, react-query.ts, task-list-item.tsx, tasks-list.tsx, create-task.ts/.tsx, get-tasks.ts); all folders are lowercase (app, routes, components, errors, layouts, ui, button, form, notifications, spinner, config, features, tasks, api, lib, types). The convention is also enforced, not just followed: .eslintrc.cjs:89-97 adds 'check-file/filename-naming-convention' KEBAB_CASE for '**/*.{ts,tsx}' and 'check-file/folder-naming-convention' KEBAB_CASE for 'src/**/!(__tests__)', with eslint-plugin-check-file added to package.json devDependencies.

expectations.text: ESLint import/no-restricted-paths boundary zones are configured, including a zone entry protecting the tasks feature
expectations.evidence: The fixture .eslintrc.cjs had no import rules at all (only react-refresh); the run's .eslintrc.cjs:31-63 adds 'import/no-restricted-paths': ['error', { zones: [...] }] with three real zones: (1) tasks-specific cross-feature block — "{ target: './src/features/tasks', from: './src/features', except: ['./tasks'] }"; (2) unidirectional flow — "{ target: './src/features', from: './src/app' }"; (3) shared-layer protection — target ['./src/components','./src/hooks','./src/lib','./src/types','./src/utils'] from ['./src/features','./src/app']. Supporting plugins (eslint-plugin-import, eslint-import-resolver-typescript) were added to package.json and the resolver/internal-regex settings are configured, so the rule can actually resolve '@/' imports.

suggestions.reason: Nothing in the assertion set checks that the result compiles or that the feature is actually wired up and reachable. An output with perfect api/ files that were never rendered would score 8/8. This run did wire it (src/app/router.tsx registers paths.app.tasks lazily, src/app/provider.tsx mounts QueryClientProvider, src/main.tsx renders <App/>, src/App.tsx deleted) — but that came for free, not because an assertion demanded it. Suggest adding: 'The tasks page is registered in the router and reachable from the app entry (App.tsx no longer contains the feature)', and, if the harness can run it, 'npm run typecheck / npm run lint passes'. Note the harness cannot currently run either — there is no node_modules in outputs/app, and the run added devDependencies (eslint-plugin-check-file, eslint-plugin-import, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, eslint-plugin-prettier, eslint-plugin-react, @types/node, prettier) that were never installed, so the committed .eslintrc.cjs is unverified as runnable.

suggestions.assertion: No barrel index.ts re-export files anywhere in the new code
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating on its own — it is satisfied by doing nothing. A lazy answer that dumps `src/api/tasks.ts` plus one component, or even leaves most code in App.tsx, passes this and the kebab-case assertion too. Consider pairing it with a positive check that imports reference deep concrete paths (e.g. '@/features/tasks/api/get-tasks'), which is what the no-barrel rule is actually for, or folding it into the folder-structure assertion.

suggestions.assertion: All new files and folders are kebab-case
suggestions.reason: Same weakness: single-word filenames trivially satisfy kebab-case, so a minimal output passes without any real convention adherence. Strengthen by requiring the convention to be enforced rather than merely observed — e.g. 'check-file/filename-naming-convention and folder-naming-convention rules are configured in ESLint' — which is a much harder bar and is what distinguishes this run.

suggestions.assertion: The create mutation validates input with an exported zod schema and its hook accepts a mutationConfig override parameter
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous phrasing: 'the create mutation validates input' can read as the fetcher/mutationFn calling schema.parse before POST, or as the schema being exported and consumed by the form. This run does the latter (createTask posts data unparsed; Form runs safeParse). I graded it PASS on the broader reading, but the assertion should say which it wants, otherwise two different implementations get inconsistent verdicts across runs.

No assertion covers the mutationConfig composition trap, which is the most common way this pattern is implemented wrongly: naively spreading '...mutationConfig' after a built-in onSuccess silently drops the caller's callback, or spreading it before drops the invalidation. This run handles it correctly (create-task.ts:34 'const { onSuccess, ...restConfig } = mutationConfig || {}' then re-invokes 'onSuccess?.(...args)' after invalidateQueries). That is a genuinely discriminating behavior worth asserting explicitly.

eval_feedback.overall: The output is substantive, not surface-compliant — every assertion is backed by real, wired-up code, and several conventions are enforced in ESLint rather than merely followed. All 8 pass. The assertion set is strong on architecture shape but weak on two axes: two assertions (no-barrels, kebab-case) are near-free to satisfy, and nothing verifies the app compiles, lints, or actually renders the feature. Adding a build/typecheck gate and a 'feature is reachable from the router' assertion would make the suite meaningfully harder to game.
